CI-06.formats: GitHub Actions workflow files `.github/workflows/*.yml|yaml` (parsed with PyYAML, never executed).
CI-06.evidence: Scope `file:<workflow path>`; static evidence quotes the first install step's lines.
CI-06.rule: A job has a dependency-install command (`npm ci|install`, `yarn`, `pnpm install`, `pip install` of a requirements/constraints file or the project itself (`-r`, `-c`, `-e .`, `.[extra]`), `poetry install`, `pipenv install|sync`, `mvn`/`mvnw`, `gradle`/`gradlew`, `bundle install`, `dotnet restore`, `cargo build|test|fetch`) and no cache evidence anywhere in the job (`actions/cache*`, a `setup-*` step with `cache`, `ruby/setup-ruby` `bundler-cache`, Gradle setup actions, `Swatinem/rust-cache`). Exceptions: job uses a local/composite action (cache may be hidden), self-hosted runner, `npm install -g`, `pip install --upgrade pip`, a single tool install such as `pip install build` (too small to cache). Confidence medium. Reported once per (job, ecosystem). Release, publish and deploy workflows and tag-triggered workflows are not evaluated (release workflows should not read caches: zizmor `cache-poisoning`). An npm install in a job with `actions/setup-node` v6+ (or an unparsable, commit-pinned version) and no `cache` input is low confidence: setup-node caches npm by itself when package.json sets `packageManager` to npm (package.json is not read). Yarn and pnpm are never cached automatically.
CI-06.unsupported: `go` modules (cache default not verified), reusable-workflow jobs (`uses:` at job level), caches configured outside the workflow (org/runner images).
CI-06.challenge: setup-node npm auto-caching via `packageManager` in package.json is invisible here and would be a false positive.

CI-07.evidence: Scope `file:<workflow path>`; static evidence quotes the build step.
CI-07.rule: A step runs `docker/build-push-action` without `cache-from`/`cache-to`, or a `run` script with `docker build` / `docker buildx build` and no cache flags. Exceptions: `no-cache: true`/`--no-cache` (deliberate clean build), scripts that pass cache flags through a variable (`CACHE_ARGS`), non-build docker commands, and a second build of the same `context` and `file` in one job (it reuses the first build's local cache). Also `docker compose build` / `docker compose up --build` and `docker/bake-action` without a cache in the step. Confidence medium for build-push-action, low for plain `docker build`, compose and bake (the compose or bake file is not read). Release, publish and deploy workflows and tag-triggered workflows are not evaluated (release workflows should not read caches: zizmor `cache-poisoning`).
CI-07.unsupported: Cache configured in the compose file (`cache_from`), the bake file, the builder or the Dockerfile (`RUN --mount=type=cache`); build time is not measured.
CI-07.challenge: A BuildKit registry cache configured via buildx environment variables is not seen.

CI-08.evidence: Scope `file:<workflow path>`; static evidence quotes the step that runs the clean build.
CI-08.rule: A non-release job restores a build-output cache (path `target`, `build`, `dist`, `out`, `.next`, `.nx`, `.turbo`; NOT keyed per run) and then runs a clean (`mvn clean`, `gradlew clean`, `make clean`, `cargo clean`, `rm -rf` of the output dir), so the cached result is thrown away. Explicit flags (`--no-build-cache`, `--rerun-tasks`, `--no-incremental`) are NOT reported: on 336 real workflow files they were deliberate every time (CodeQL and Infer need a fresh compile, forced test runs, dependency warm-ups). Exceptions: a cache keyed per run (`github.run_id`, `github.sha`) is a hand-off between jobs; `.gradle` (project task history) is not removed by `clean`; release/publish/deploy jobs and tag workflows. Confidence medium. Static only.
CI-08.unsupported: Tools with their own remote caches are not evaluated (Turborepo, Nx Cloud, Bazel). Build duration is not measured.
CI-08.challenge: A clean build before a release-candidate PR check may be required for reproducibility.

CI-10.evidence: Scope `file:<workflow path>`; static evidence quotes the first test step of the job.
CI-10.rule: The workflow runs on `pull_request` with no `paths`/`paths-ignore`, or on `push` with no branch/tag/path filter at all, and a job runs a test command (`pytest`, `npm test`, `go test`, `mvn test|verify`, `gradle test`, `cargo test`, `jest`, `vitest`, `rspec`, `dotnet test`, `make test`, `tox`, `nox`); installing a test tool (`pip install pytest`) is not running tests. Exceptions: path filters, test selection (`--onlyChanged`, `--changedSince`, `--testmon`, `nx affected`), `dorny/paths-filter` or `tj-actions/changed-files`, a job or step gated by an `if` on changes or on other jobs'/steps' outputs, schedule/dispatch-only, tag-only and branch-limited push workflows. Confidence low: required status checks may need the workflow to run on every change (UNVERIFIED: branch-protection interaction). GitHub documents that a required status check whose workflow is skipped by path/branch/commit-message filters stays Pending and blocks merging (verified), so the finding recommends job-level change detection when the workflow may be required. The taxonomy's own note: skipping tests by path risks missing tests the change needs.
CI-10.unsupported: History half dropped: the run/job objects carry no changed-file lists, so docs-only runs cannot be confirmed.
CI-10.challenge: A required status check configured on this workflow would block merges if a path filter skipped it.

CI-11.formats: GitHub Actions workflow YAML (`on` as string, list or mapping).
CI-11.evidence: Scope `file:<workflow path>`; static evidence quotes the `on:` entry, the `push:` entry or the `concurrency:` entry.
CI-11.rule: (1) `push` with no branch/tag/path filter plus `pull_request`: every PR commit runs twice. (2) A `pull_request` workflow with no `concurrency` at workflow or job level: superseded runs keep running. (3) `concurrency` set without `cancel-in-progress`: GitHub only queues. Exceptions: `workflow_call`-only, `pull_request_target` automation, `pull_request` with `types` that leave out `synchronize` (no run is ever superseded), workflows with an `environment` job or a deploy/release/publish name (never cancel deployments), an explicit `cancel-in-progress: false` (deliberate queue), `cancel-in-progress` given as an expression. (4, low confidence: only one file is read) A cancelling `concurrency.group` (workflow or job level) made only of context expressions with no `github.workflow` and no literal text, for example `${{ github.ref }}`: another workflow with the same group cancels it. A group with literal text is assumed unique. Confidence: (2) high, (1) and (3) medium, (4) low.
CI-11.unsupported: Whether the push and PR branches actually overlap when a branch filter exists. Reusable workflows called from elsewhere.
CI-11.challenge: Two workflows that both use the same literal group name still cancel each other; groups are only judged inside one file.

CI-13.formats: GitHub Actions workflow YAML with `strategy.matrix` mappings.
CI-13.evidence: Scope `file:<workflow path>`; static evidence quotes the `matrix:` entry (first 8 lines).
CI-13.rule: (a) a duplicate value in a matrix axis (high), (b) an `include` entry whose keys are all axis keys with values already in the axes, so it adds no job (medium). Wide matrices are deliberately NOT reported: in real repositories (pandas, next.js) they are intentional support matrices. Dynamic matrices (`fromJSON`) are not evaluated and the limitation is stated. actionlint already reports duplicate matrix values (verified); the no-op `include` rule is ours.
CI-13.unsupported: Matrices built at runtime; whether a combination is actually needed (wide matrices are not reported).
CI-13.challenge: A deliberate duplicate axis value used as a retry slot would be reported.
